open_obligations: Note that Reppert et al. do not distil the decomposition into a single model as Iterated Amplification does.
Check that the developer had gold answers throughout, which Iterated Amplification does not assume.
Check whether the decompositions are deep enough to bear on beyond-human-scale tasks.
in.other_title: Iterated decomposition: human-in-the-loop workflow for refining compositional LM programs
in.rationale: Christiano et al. state their experiments use a hand-coded decomposer on algorithmic tasks and shed no light on whether humans can decompose real-world tasks. Reppert et al. report human developers iteratively decomposing real science Q&A tasks, raising held-out accuracy (placebo description 25% to 65%, adherence 53% to 70%, Qasper 38% to 69%); the decompositions are hand-designed LM programs, not trained by amplification and distillation.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether humans can decompose interesting real-world tasks for LM pipelines, on science Q&A tasks from the Elicit assistant

text: The authors state that in their experiments questions are algorithmically decomposable and the human is replaced with a hand-coded algorithm, so the experiments shed no light on whether humans can decompose interesting real-world tasks or whether messy real-world decompositions can be learned. They also note the combinatorial domains admit an algorithmic training signal, unlike the tasks they ultimately care about.
title: Experiments use hand-coded algorithmic decompositions, not humans
